meta.title: TORFL A1 Elementary — Russian
meta.subtitle: 500 words · both directions, as two cards per word
meta.desc: Both study directions in one deck: Russian → English (see the Russian, recall the meaning) and English → Russian (see an English meaning, recall the Russian). Each direction is a card of its own with its own schedule, so recognising a word and producing it are learnt separately. 500 words for the Elementary level (Элементарный уровень, ТЭУ) of TORFL, the Test of Russian as a Foreign Language (ТРКИ), the Russian state examination, which corresponds to CEFR A1. TORFL's Elementary level is aligned to A1 of the Common European Framework of Reference, whose global descriptor begins 'Can understand and use familiar everyday expressions and very basic phrases aimed at the satisfaction of needs of a concrete type' — a learner here is able to introduce themselves and others, to ask and answer questions about personal details such as where they live, people they know and things they have, and to interact in a simple way provided the other person talks slowly and clearly and is prepared to help. WHERE THESE WORDS COME FROM, since it matters: TORFL's lexical minimum for each level is published as a book under copyright rather than as an open list, so this deck is not the exam board's vocabulary and does not claim to be. It is assembled from two things that can be stated. 345 of the 500 come from a vocabulary written for the level's scope — greetings and politeness, introducing yourself, family, numbers, telling the time, days and months, food and drink, shopping and money, the home, the town and getting about, the body and feeling ill, the weather, colours, and the pronouns, question words, prepositions and conjunctions every sentence is built out of — and the other 155 are the commonest remaining words of everyday Russian, taken from a frequency list built from film and television subtitles and counted by the WHOLE word, every case and every tense added together, since a list of word forms ranks книгу above книга. The cards are dealt by that frequency, so the words you meet most often come first. Every headword and every form is printed with its stress mark, as Russian dictionaries for learners print them, because Russian stress is free and moves (рука́, ру́ку) and nothing in the spelling shows it; the example sentences are printed as they were written, without stress. 80 of the verbs are taught as aspect pairs on one card, imperfective first (де́лать / сде́лать), each with its own conjugation, since a Russian verb is learnt as a pair; the verbs of motion that make round trips (ходи́ть, е́здить) are cards of their own beside идти́ and е́хать, because the difference is the lesson. The 184 nouns show their gender, their genitive singular and their nominative plural, from which the rest of the declension follows, and every word that inflects has its whole table behind the All forms fold. 9 of the entries are set phrases rather than single words — потому что, меня зовут, как дела. Every word carries three real example sentences, with the word picked out in colour and a speaker beside the sentence and the headword. There is no transliteration: learn the alphabet first with the Russian alphabet deck, which is the first deck in this collection. Sources. Level: the Common European Framework of Reference (Council of Europe), global scale. Meanings, forms, stress and aspect: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). Frequency: a word list built from OpenSubtitles (hermitdave/FrequencyWords, CC BY-SA 4.0). Example sentences: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR.
